hook.text: The most powerful earthquake in US history — magnitude 9.2 — hit Alaska on Good Friday 1964.

buildup.text: The ground shook for over four minutes. Entire neighborhoods dropped 30 feet in landslides.

discovery.text: Liquefaction destroyed Turnagain Heights — homes slid on a layer of liquidized clay.

twist.text: Tsunamis generated by the quake killed people as far away as Crescent City, California.

climax.text: Only 131 died — Alaska's low population density was the saving factor, not engineering.

punchline.text: Nature delivered its most powerful blow. Sparse population was the only defense.

quiz.question: What made the 1964 Alaska earthquake the most powerful in US history?
options: It caused more deaths than any other US earthquake
At magnitude 9.2, it released more energy than any other recorded US quake
It destroyed more buildings than any earthquake in the world

details.summary: The 1964 Great Alaska Earthquake, magnitude 9.2, was the second-largest earthquake ever recorded and lasted over four minutes. It generated devastating tsunamis, caused widespread landslides and ground subsidence over 250,000 square kilometers.
details.whyItMatters: The 1964 Alaska earthquake advanced understanding of megathrust subduction zone earthquakes and tsunami generation, leading to the creation of the Pacific Tsunami Warning System and modern tsunami science.
takeaways: At magnitude 9.2, it was the second-largest earthquake ever instrumentally recorded
Ground deformation affected over 250,000 square kilometers of terrain
The tsunami caused more deaths than the shaking itself, even reaching California

faq.question: How did the 1964 Alaska earthquake change our understanding of plate tectonics?
faq.answer: The earthquake confirmed the megathrust model where the Pacific Plate subducts beneath the North American Plate. The rupture area extended over 800 kilometers. Measured ground deformation provided direct evidence of plate boundary mechanics.

faq.question: What damage did liquefaction and landslides cause during the 1964 earthquake?
faq.answer: Entire neighborhoods in Anchorage collapsed into landslide-displaced blocks as sensitive clay layers liquefied. The Turnagain Heights landslide destroyed 75 homes. Downtown Anchorage subsided and cracked.
